description: The Musical of Musicals (The Musical!) is a musical about musicals! In this hilarious satire of musical theatre, one story becomes five delightful musicals, each written in the distinctive style of a different master of the form, from Rodgers and Hammerstein to Stephen Sondheim. The basic plot: June is an ingenue who can't pay the rent and is threatened by her evil landlord. Will the handsome leading man come to the rescue? The variations are: a Rodgers & Hammerstein version, set in Kansas in August, complete with a dream ballet; a Sondheim version, featuring the landlord as a tortured artistic genius who slashes the throats of his tenants in revenge for not appreciating his work; a Jerry Herman version, as a splashy star vehicle; an Andrew Lloyd Webber version, a rock musical with themes borrowed from Puccini; and a Kander & Ebb version, set in a speakeasy in Chicago. This comic valentine to musical theatre was the longest running show in the York Theatre Company's 35-year history before moving to Off-Broadway.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: Musical of Musicals (The Musical!)

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.

description: The Musical of Musicals (The Musical!) is a musical about musicals! In this hilarious satire of musical theatre, one story becomes five delightful musicals, each written in the distinctive style of a different master of the form, from Rodgers and Hammerstein to Stephen Sondheim. The basic plot: June is an ingenue who can't pay the rent and is threatened by her evil landlord. Will the handsome leading man come to the rescue? The variations are: a Rodgers & Hammerstein version, set in Kansas in August, complete with a dream ballet; a Sondheim version, featuring the landlord as a tortured artistic genius who slashes the throats of his tenants in revenge for not appreciating his work; a Jerry Herman version, as a splashy star vehicle; an Andrew Lloyd Webber version, a rock musical with themes borrowed from Puccini; and a Kander & Ebb version, set in a speakeasy in Chicago. This comic valentine to musical theatre was the longest running show in the York Theatre Company's 35-year history before moving to Off-Broadway.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: Musical of Musicals (The Musical!)

description: Dr. Temple Grandin has been called “the most accomplished and well-known adult with autism in the world.” Her autism has given her a unique perspective into the lives of stock animals, and half of the cattle in the U.S. are handled in facilities designed by Grandin. She has authored six books, and her life is the subject of a recent HBO film and a BBC documentary, "The Woman Who Thinks Like a Cow." She will provide insight into her life’s challenges and successes, and provide insight into what the New York Times calls “a mind that’s ‘different but not less.’”

name: A Memoir of My Life with Animals and Autism

description: The Musical of Musicals (The Musical!) is a musical about musicals! In this hilarious satire of musical theatre, one story becomes five delightful musicals, each written in the distinctive style of a different master of the form, from Rodgers and Hammerstein to Stephen Sondheim. The basic plot: June is an ingenue who can't pay the rent and is threatened by her evil landlord. Will the handsome leading man come to the rescue? The variations are: a Rodgers & Hammerstein version, set in Kansas in August, complete with a dream ballet; a Sondheim version, featuring the landlord as a tortured artistic genius who slashes the throats of his tenants in revenge for not appreciating his work; a Jerry Herman version, as a splashy star vehicle; an Andrew Lloyd Webber version, a rock musical with themes borrowed from Puccini; and a Kander & Ebb version, set in a speakeasy in Chicago. This comic valentine to musical theatre was the longest running show in the York Theatre Company's 35-year history before moving to Off-Broadway.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: Musical of Musicals (The Musical!)

The variations are: a Rodgers & Hammerstein version, set in Kansas in August, complete with a dream ballet; a Sondheim version, featuring the landlord as a tortured artistic genius who slashes the throats of his tenants in revenge for not appreciating his work; a Jerry Herman version, as a splashy star vehicle; an Andrew Lloyd Webber version, a rock musical with themes borrowed from Puccini; and a Kander & Ebb version, set in a speakeasy in Chicago. This comic valentine to musical theatre was the longest running show in the York Theatre Company's 35-year history before moving to Off-Broadway.

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

This new and exciting event for children and their parent, grandparent or special adult will be held from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Drury University’s O’Reilly Family Event Center. This includes lunch and a powerpak for each child. Registration is required. To learn more about all the fun activities and a time schedule for the stage performances and special events, and to make your registration please visit www.commpartnership.org or call Community Partnership at 888-2020.

description: Social critic, political commentator, author and TV host Bill Maher, who for the last seventeen years has set the boundaries of where funny political talk can go on American television, makes his way to Springfield, Missouri for a live appearance at Juanita K. Hammons Hall for the Performing Arts on March 20 at 7:30 p.m. First on Politically Incorrect (Comedy Central, ABC, 1993-2002) and for the last eight years on HBO’s Real Time, Maher’s combination of unflinching honesty and big laughs have garnered him twenty-six Emmy nominations. In October of 2008, this same combination was on display in Maher’s uproarious and unprecedented swipe at organized religion, Religulous, directed by Larry Charles (Borat). The documentary has gone on to become the 7th Highest Grossing Documentary ever. In addition to his television program – which has featured such regular visitors as John Edwards, Ben Affleck, Robin Williams, Arianna Huffington, Alec Baldwin and Michael Moore – Maher has written four bestsellers: “True Story,” “Does Anybody Have a Problem with That? Politically Incorrect’s Greatest Hits,” “When You Ride Alone, You Ride with Bin Laden” and most recently, “New Rules: Polite Musings from a Timid Observer.” Maher started his career as a stand-up comedian in 1979, and still performs at least fifty dates a year in Las Vegas and in sold out theaters all across the country. Three of his nine stand-up specials for HBO – 2007’s “The Decider,” 2005’s “I’m Swiss,” as well as his most recent, the hilarious, “Bill Maher … But I’m Not Wrong,” – have been nominated for Emmy awards. Maher was born in New York City, raised in River Vale, N.J. and went to Cornell University. He now resides in Los Angeles. Tickets to his MSU show are priced at $50 and $65, and can be purchased at Missouri State TIX locations, online at
name: Bill Maher Performs at Juanita K. Hammons Hall

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description: This popular annual event showcases an impressive array of original works performed by a large company of dancers. description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description: University Heights Baptist Church will continue its First Wednesday Noon Concert Series with a concert featuring the music of Julie Combs in the Chapel at 12:10 p.m. Wednesday, March 2. Julie Combs is the head of the department of music at Missouri State University. Before assuming that role, she was at the Oklahoma State University Music Department as department head and professor. She also taught oboe, music theory and music history at the University of Wyoming. Before her academic career, Combs was the fourth woman accepted as a member of The United States Army Band "Pershing's Own" in Washington, D.C., where she was principal oboe with the U.S. Army Chamber Orchestra. Combs holds a Bachelor of Music in woodwinds (oboe performance) and a Master of Music (oboe performance) with performer's certificate from the University of Memphis. She completed her Doctor of Musical Arts degree at the University of North Texas, where she performed on both the modern and baroque oboes. She has performed regularly as a soloist, chamber musician and orchestral oboist on the oboe, oboe d'amore and English horn.
name: Dr. Julie Combs In Concert

She also taught oboe, music theory and music history at the University of Wyoming. Before her academic career, Combs was the fourth woman accepted as a member of The United States Army Band "Pershing's Own" in Washington, D.C., where she was principal oboe with the U.S. Army Chamber Orchestra. Combs holds a Bachelor of Music in woodwinds (oboe performance) and a Master of Music (oboe performance) with performer's certificate from the University of Memphis. She completed her Doctor of Musical Arts degree at the University of North Texas, where she performed on both the modern and baroque oboes. She has performed regularly as a soloist, chamber musician and orchestral oboist on the oboe, oboe d'amore and English horn.
name: Dr. Julie Combs In Concert

“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

description: University Heights Baptist Church will continue its First Wednesday Noon Concert Series with a concert featuring the music of Julie Combs in the Chapel at 12:10 p.m. Wednesday, March 2. Julie Combs is the head of the department of music at Missouri State University. Before assuming that role, she was at the Oklahoma State University Music Department as department head and professor. She also taught oboe, music theory and music history at the University of Wyoming. Before her academic career, Combs was the fourth woman accepted as a member of The United States Army Band "Pershing's Own" in Washington, D.C., where she was principal oboe with the U.S. Army Chamber Orchestra. Combs holds a Bachelor of Music in woodwinds (oboe performance) and a Master of Music (oboe performance) with performer's certificate from the University of Memphis. She completed her Doctor of Musical Arts degree at the University of North Texas, where she performed on both the modern and baroque oboes. She has performed regularly as a soloist, chamber musician and orchestral oboist on the oboe, oboe d'amore and English horn.
name: Dr. Julie Combs In Concert

description: Social critic, political commentator, author and TV host Bill Maher, who for the last seventeen years has set the boundaries of where funny political talk can go on American television, makes his way to Springfield, Missouri for a live appearance at Juanita K. Hammons Hall for the Performing Arts on March 20 at 7:30 p.m. First on Politically Incorrect (Comedy Central, ABC, 1993-2002) and for the last eight years on HBO’s Real Time, Maher’s combination of unflinching honesty and big laughs have garnered him twenty-six Emmy nominations. In October of 2008, this same combination was on display in Maher’s uproarious and unprecedented swipe at organized religion, Religulous, directed by Larry Charles (Borat). The documentary has gone on to become the 7th Highest Grossing Documentary ever. In addition to his television program – which has featured such regular visitors as John Edwards, Ben Affleck, Robin Williams, Arianna Huffington, Alec Baldwin and Michael Moore – Maher has written four bestsellers: “True Story,” “Does Anybody Have a Problem with That? Politically Incorrect’s Greatest Hits,” “When You Ride Alone, You Ride with Bin Laden” and most recently, “New Rules: Polite Musings from a Timid Observer.” Maher started his career as a stand-up comedian in 1979, and still performs at least fifty dates a year in Las Vegas and in sold out theaters all across the country. Three of his nine stand-up specials for HBO – 2007’s “The Decider,” 2005’s “I’m Swiss,” as well as his most recent, the hilarious, “Bill Maher … But I’m Not Wrong,” – have been nominated for Emmy awards. Maher was born in New York City, raised in River Vale, N.J. and went to Cornell University. He now resides in Los Angeles. Tickets to his MSU show are priced at $50 and $65, and can be purchased at Missouri State TIX locations, online at
name: Bill Maher Performs at Juanita K. Hammons Hall

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

On the 99th anniversary of Titanic’s maiden voyage, amateur (HAM) radio operators will band together worldwide for a very special broadcast originating from Titanic Museum Attraction. The event will commemorate the anniversary of the sinking and will honor the two wireless operators, Jack Phillips and Harold Bride, who sent distress signals into the early morning hours of April 15, 1912. HAM operators from Branson to Belfast, Northern Ireland, will transmit news of the anniversary using a special call sign and signals. Visitors are invited to witness this live event, which offers a firsthand look at the fragile and primitive nature of communications at sea in 1912.

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description:
“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.
name: Biggest Loser Pound for Pound Challenge

On the 99th anniversary of Titanic’s maiden voyage, amateur (HAM) radio operators will band together worldwide for a very special broadcast originating from Titanic Museum Attraction. The event will commemorate the anniversary of the sinking and will honor the two wireless operators, Jack Phillips and Harold Bride, who sent distress signals into the early morning hours of April 15, 1912. HAM operators from Branson to Belfast, Northern Ireland, will transmit news of the anniversary using a special call sign and signals. Visitors are invited to witness this live event, which offers a firsthand look at the fragile and primitive nature of communications at sea in 1912.

description: Social critic, political commentator, author and TV host Bill Maher, who for the last seventeen years has set the boundaries of where funny political talk can go on American television, makes his way to Springfield, Missouri for a live appearance at Juanita K. Hammons Hall for the Performing Arts on March 20 at 7:30 p.m. First on Politically Incorrect (Comedy Central, ABC, 1993-2002) and for the last eight years on HBO’s Real Time, Maher’s combination of unflinching honesty and big laughs have garnered him twenty-six Emmy nominations. In October of 2008, this same combination was on display in Maher’s uproarious and unprecedented swipe at organized religion, Religulous, directed by Larry Charles (Borat). The documentary has gone on to become the 7th Highest Grossing Documentary ever. In addition to his television program – which has featured such regular visitors as John Edwards, Ben Affleck, Robin Williams, Arianna Huffington, Alec Baldwin and Michael Moore – Maher has written four bestsellers: “True Story,” “Does Anybody Have a Problem with That? Politically Incorrect’s Greatest Hits,” “When You Ride Alone, You Ride with Bin Laden” and most recently, “New Rules: Polite Musings from a Timid Observer.” Maher started his career as a stand-up comedian in 1979, and still performs at least fifty dates a year in Las Vegas and in sold out theaters all across the country. Three of his nine stand-up specials for HBO – 2007’s “The Decider,” 2005’s “I’m Swiss,” as well as his most recent, the hilarious, “Bill Maher … But I’m Not Wrong,” – have been nominated for Emmy awards. Maher was born in New York City, raised in River Vale, N.J. and went to Cornell University. He now resides in Los Angeles. Tickets to his MSU show are priced at $50 and $65, and can be purchased at Missouri State TIX locations, online at

“The Biggest Loser” fans can help feed Ozarkers in need this year by participating in the show’s Pound for Pound Challenge, a program that encourages residents in Missouri and people across the country to lose weight nationally to help provide hunger relief locally. 

The Pound for Pound Challenge, which grew out of the success of “The Biggest Loser,” is back for its third year. For every pound individuals pledge to lose now through May 31, 2011, 11 cents will be donated to Feeding America, which distributes the money directly to member food banks—including Ozarks Food Harvest—based on ZIP codes. Last year, nearly $5,000 was raised for Ozarks Food Harvest through the Pound for Pound Challenge, up $3,000 from the first year. Those wishing to pledge their weight loss goals online can log on at pfpchallenge.com. Each pound pledged equals one pound of food purchased for hungry southwest Missouri families. Those already at a healthy weight range can participate by pledging to maintain, up to a donation of five pounds of food. Season 11 of “The Biggest Loser” premiered Jan. 4 at 7 p.m. on NBC. Participants can share their stories at facebook.com/poundforpoundchallenge. Learn more at ozarksfoodharvest.org and at facebook.com/ozarksfoodharvest.

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

Earth Day Begins at Home: Earth Day Green Building Fair April 16

Springfield, MO – Homeowners can learn how their homes affect the environment and how to green them up at the Earth Day Green Building Fair Saturday, April 16. It’s all free to the public from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. at The Library Center, 4653 S. Campbell, Springfield.

Sponsored by the Ozarks Green Building Coalition, the fair will feature five presentations in the auditorium from noon to 5 p.m., as well as exhibits in the concourse from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.  Exhibits will cover the basics of green building, including a home energy audit, the first step in improving a home’s energy efficiency. Exhibits also will include alternative energy options, new ideas in green developments and information about buying and selling green homes. Information will be available on programs to help pay for green renovations and the latest on green building materials and services in the Springfield area.

The five presentations are:

“Building a Green Home: A Homeowner’s Perspective.” 12 p.m.  Matt O’Reilly, whose Green Circle Shopping Center on Republic Road is arguably the greenest shopping center in the U.S. has built a green home. He will share his family’s experience navigating the maze of building regulations, opportunities for building a greener home and options for certification.

“How Green is Your Home?” 1 p.m.  Participants can take a short quiz and learn how their homes rank on a green scale. They also can learn what makes the greenest homes winners and how green features are rated by realtors in Springfield who help buy and sell green homes. Presenters are Mary Mike Taylor, Mary Mike and Associates; Zach Miller, Murney Associates REALTORS; and Sam Butler, SustainaBuilt Construction.

“What’s New in Alternative Energy for the Home?”  2 p.m. Participants can learn about new developments in solar, wind and geothermal energy sources for homes. Zeke Fairbank of The Alternative Energy CO. and Rory Krueger of Krueger Mechanical Services will explain how to take advantage of  alternative energy’s declining costs and increasing efficiency to reduce energy bills for years to come.

“Making Green Homes Affordable: Great Ways to Save.” 3 p.m. Korina Branson of Greenstick, LLC and Jeff Barber, architect, University of Missouri Extension, will discuss federal, state and utility programs; tax incentives; and  rebates designed to help with the initial cost of making homes more energy efficient. They’ll also uncover the hidden savings in green construction, which allow homebuyers to choose green options at little or no additional cost or, in some cases, while actually saving money.

“Beyond Rain Barrels.”  4 p.m. Presenters Dan Chiles, Emerald Ops, and Stuart Murr, Smart Designs, will explore the latest in cisterns and graywater systems for the home.  These options go beyond capturing rainwater in barrels and offer additional ways to save and recycle water, thereby protecting our region’s water supplies and those of the homeowner.

 OGBC is a nonprofit organization incorporated in 2007 whose mission is to promote green building by increasing public and professional knowledge and awareness of the benefits of green building.  Members of the Coalition include builders, contractors, appraisers, lenders, interior designers, landscape architects, real estate professionals, architects and engineers, city and county representatives and members of professional building and environmental groups. For more information, go to

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description: The play tells the story of two young bucks who, having spent all their money by living too well, leave London and roam from town to town in search of love and fortune. In order to find a wealthy heiress for at least one of them, they pose as master and servant – exchanging roles from one town to the next. In Lichfield, Aimwell is the master and Archer the servant, and there they meet the lovely, wealthy Dorinda and her equally desirable sister-in-law, Mrs. Kate Sullen. They set their caps for these women, but problems abound. Kate is married to a drunken sot who despises her; the innkeeper’s saucy daughter, Cherry, has set her cap for Archer; Dorinda’s mother, Lady Bountiful, mistakenly believes herself to be a great healer of the sick, and she guards her daughter like a dragoness; and a band of brigands plans to rob the house of Lady Bountiful that very night, putting all schemes in jeopardy. This is a play in the great tradition of Goldsmith’s She Stoops to Conquer and Sheridan’s The Rivals and The School for Scandal. It is classic, formal, robust and hilarious.
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall
name: The Beaux Stratagem

description:
Music and lyrics by Stephen Schwartz. Book by John Caird. Children of Eden is a joyous and inspirational musical about parents, children and faith…not to mention centuries of unresolved family business! Loosely based on the Book of Genesis, Children of Eden is a frank, heartfelt and often humorous examination of the age-old conflict between parents and children. Adam, Eve, Noah and the “Father” who created them deal with the headstrong, cataclysmic actions of their respective children. The show ultimately delivers a bittersweet message: that “the hardest part of love…is letting go.”

description: Critics and peers agree: Brian Regan has distinguished himself as one of the premier comedians in the country. Written by Larry Shue. Charlie, painfully shy, socially awkward Englishman, agrees to accompany his friend, Froggy, to a Georgia fishing lodge while Froggy conducts his annual demolition class at a nearby army base. To protect his super shy friend from unwanted social interaction, Froggy passes Charlie off as a foreigner who neither speaks nor understands English. description: Critics and peers agree: Brian Regan has distinguished himself as one of the premier comedians in the country. The perfect balance of sophisticated writing and physicality, Brian fills theaters nationwide with fervent fans that span generations. Releasing two critically acclaimed hour Comedy Central specials and DVD's in as many years - 2008's "The Epitome of Hyperbole," and 2007's "Brian Regan Standing Up" - Brian has set a standard of excellence that others continually try to follow. Brian's non-stop theater tour has visited more than 80 cities each year since 2005 and continues through 2010. It is the quality of his material, relatable to a wide audience and revered by his peers, which continues to grow Brian's fan base. In March Brian will set the record for most consecutive shows by a comedian at Abravanal Hall in Salt Lake City with five sold out performances. The previous record was four shows set by Jerry Seinfeld in 2005. With his first appearance on "The Late Show with David Letterman" in 1995, Brian solidified his place on the show and has now made more than 20 appearances. He also includes regular visits with Conan O'Brien on his schedule. A dorm room favorite, Brian's 1997 CD, "Brian Regan Live," has sold over 150,000 copies and consistently charts in iTunes Top Ten Comedy Albums. Brian's 2000 "Comedy Central Presents" special continues to be a top viewer choice and Brian's independently released 2004 DVD, "I Walked on the Moon," is available at www.BrianRegan.com
name: Brian Regan Live!

The most produced play in American theatre history, “Our Town” centers on the life of Grovers Corners, a northeast farm community. Charlie, painfully shy, socially awkward Englishman, agrees to accompany his friend, Froggy, to a Georgia fishing lodge while Froggy conducts his annual demolition class at a nearby army base. To protect his super shy friend from unwanted social interaction, Froggy passes Charlie off as a foreigner who neither speaks nor understands English. Because of this, people feel no need to censor their conversations in front of him and so, Charlie’s disguise exposes everybody’s peccadilloes. description: Critics and peers agree: Brian Regan has distinguished himself as one of the premier comedians in the country. The perfect balance of sophisticated writing and physicality, Brian fills theaters nationwide with fervent fans that span generations. Releasing two critically acclaimed hour Comedy Central specials and DVD's in as many years - 2008's "The Epitome of Hyperbole," and 2007's "Brian Regan Standing Up" - Brian has set a standard of excellence that others continually try to follow. Brian's non-stop theater tour has visited more than 80 cities each year since 2005 and continues through 2010. It is the quality of his material, relatable to a wide audience and revered by his peers, which continues to grow Brian's fan base. In March Brian will set the record for most consecutive shows by a comedian at Abravanal Hall in Salt Lake City with five sold out performances. The previous record was four shows set by Jerry Seinfeld in 2005. With his first appearance on "The Late Show with David Letterman" in 1995, Brian solidified his place on the show and has now made more than 20 appearances. He also includes regular visits with Conan O'Brien on his schedule. A dorm room favorite, Brian's 1997 CD, "Brian Regan Live," has sold over 150,000 copies and consistently charts in iTunes Top Ten Comedy Albums. Brian's 2000 "Comedy Central Presents" special continues to be a top viewer choice and Brian's independently released 2004 DVD, "I Walked on the Moon," is available at www.BrianRegan.com
name: Brian Regan Live!

description:
Considered an indie on a major. Formed in 1997 after youngest sibling wrote their first song at age 8, were given opportunity to perform/grow in local coffee house/rock venue, played 100's of shows as unsigned indie for 4 years ('98 - '02) until grabbing their first Nat'l fan-base at Cornerstone Fest' in Summer '02 followed by an invitation from friends in Midlake to open at a 21+ bar, giving them visibility to the many clubs in DFW - positioning them for a prime slot at the Dallas New Music Festival in Fall '02 where the Deep Ellum movers / shakers attended.

2 EP's + 2 Full Lengths (+ several B-side) later, Eisley's steady growth and credibility as writers / performers comes from the live side (touring). The band's undaunted commitment to their own unique, visually imaginative brand has, perhaps, curbed access to mass homogenized portals such as FM radio, though, single - "Telescope Eyes" charted on Dallas rock radio (102.1 The Edge) as 24th most played song in 2003.

The Winery opened 2 years ago and produces wine and mead (wine made from honey). description: Area families are invited to enjoy free kids' activities, live music and BBQ at the 5th Annual Community Awareness Fair, all while learning about services that help keep families strong and kids healthy. The event, to be held at Jordan Valley Park on Saturday, June 11, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., includes organizations ready to connect families with community resources such as after-school activities, youth mentoring, parental support, counseling services and drug-prevention programs. This free event is sponsored by CASA Southwest Missouri and the Greene County Juvenile Office, along with Reclaiming Futures. Organizations and interested vendors should contact Jill Randolph, Greene County Juvenile Office, at 417-829-6151.

description:

All participants receive a t-shirt, ticket to the Springfield Cardinals game that evening, and admittance to the pre-game activities (crafts, bounce house, talent show, Xbox Kinect games, resource fair, face painting, etc.).

This event shows the public that we want the same things for our kids that everyone wants - equal opportunities and inclusion in all activities. We are more alike than different!

EVERYONE is welcome at this event whether you know someone with Down Syndrome or not!

description: Tent Theatre and Missouri State University presents: OKLAHOMA!  Music by Richard Rodgers Book and Lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II  Based on the play "Green Grow the Lilacs" by Lynn Riggs July 6-9, 11-17   Rodgers & Hammerstein's first collaboration remains, in many ways, their most innovative, having set the standards and established the rules of musical theatre still being followed today. Set in a Western Indian territory just after the turn of the century, the high-spirited rivalry between the local farmers and cowboys provides the colorful background against which Curly, a handsome cowboy, and Laurey, a winsome farm girl, play out their love story. Although the road to true love never runs smooth, with these two headstrong romantics holding the reins, love's journey is as bumpy as a surrey ride down a country road. That they will succeed in making a new life together we have no doubt, and that this new life will begin in a brand-new state provides the ultimate climax to the triumphant OKLAHOMA!
venue: Missouri State University - Craig Hall

In almost non-stop song and dance, Once On This Island Junior tells the story of Ti Moune, a peasant girl who rescues and falls in love with Daniel, a weathly boy from the other side of her island.
